dedupe_keys.name: itu r report bt 2386 0 digital terrestrial broadcasting design and implementation of single frequency networks 2015

description: Report ITU-R BT.2386-0 (July 2015) is a 176-page guide to designing and implementing single frequency networks (SFN), in which all transmitters in a service area broadcast the same programme on one frequency. It analyses benefits and drawbacks of SFNs, stating that they save spectrum but do not solve rising spectrum demand, and it gives many practical examples. A general part covers concepts common to all standards, followed by parts for the DVB and DAB family (propagation and scattering, optimisation, timing, distribution, large SFN and T2-Lite), ISDB and DTMB, with the emphasis on designs, implementations and case studies. Producer: ITU-R Study Group 6 (Geneva). Coverage: worldwide practice across the three ITU regions. Access: the PDF downloads from the ITU server without login. Licence and cost: free to download; the cover page states ITU copyright with all rights reserved. Caveats: it is a 2015 edition, so newer standards updates are not included, and the network examples are described, not released as data. Simulation uses: the parameters and case studies support validation of broadcast coverage and capacity planning models. Related records: EBU Tech 3391 on DAB network planning (data-ebu-tech-3391-dab-network-planning-guidelines) and ITU-R P.1546 (model-itu-r-p-1546).
